commit.message:
ranking: add --all-tickers to score every priced name, bypassing sector filter

The rank-as-of funnel resolved candidates from nasdaq_hc_tech_universe(), which
only returns tickers with a cached `sector` row — so names with prices and
fundamentals but no classification were silently dropped (38 scored out of ~1,600).

--all-tickers skips fetch_listed_symbols() and classify_and_cache() entirely and
scores every ticker that has price data (field='close') in the store. No-peek is
intact: candidate enumeration uses the new PITStore.tickers_with_field(), but each
candidate is still scored through get_data(..., as_of). Fails loud on an empty store
rather than emitting a blank ranking. Guarding evals land with the logic.

commit.message:
universe: backfill sector classification for fundamentals-only tickers

When fundamentals are ingested for many tickers but classify_and_cache ran over a
smaller subset, most names have quality rows yet no sector row — and the ranking
funnel only scores names with a sector row, so they are silently excluded.

Add backfill_sectors.py: finds every ticker with a fundamental field in pit_records
but no sector row, then runs classify_and_cache over exactly that set (SimFin
company+industry reference, no network unless --refresh). In-scope tech/healthcare
names get cached; out-of-scope (financials/energy) are correctly left unclassified.

Guarded by tests/test_backfill_sectors.py (offline, injected reference loader):
candidate selection excludes already-classified and prices-only names; backfill
classifies and expands the universe; no-op when everything is already classified.

commit.message:
data: use refresh_days=36500 sentinel so cached SimFin zips are never re-downloaded

When refresh=False the SimFin library was re-fetching bulk CSVs if the cached
files were older than 30 days (the previous default). Switch to 36500 (100 years)
so valid cached zips are always used without hitting the API again. refresh=True
keeps refresh_days=0 (force re-download). Also wire refresh_days into
load_companies and load_industries, which previously inherited the library default
(30 days) and could trigger unexpected network calls during classify_and_cache.

commit.message:
data: treat blank/unparseable SimFin Publish Date as missing so the fallback fires (#34)

* data: treat blank/unparseable SimFin Publish Date as missing so the fallback fires

PR #33 added a Report-Date+lag fallback for a missing Publish Date, but gated it on
pd.isna(publish). SimFin's FREE bulk ships Publish Date as an EMPTY STRING, not NaT:
pd.isna("") is False, so the fallback never fired on the real ingest path. The blank
string fell through to pd.Timestamp("") -> NaT, and the not-null schema rejected the
rows -> no fundamentals stored -> quality n/a in production, even though the NaT
fixture passed. The diagnostic's .isna() check missed it too ("0/24 Publish Date NaT").

Fix: _coerce_date() turns NaN / NaT / None / "" / whitespace / unparseable into None
(value is coerced via pd.to_numeric too), so records_from_frames detects a truly
missing Publish Date and applies the no-peek-safe knowledge_date = period end + lag.
A present, parseable Publish Date is still used verbatim. Piotroski math untouched.

Diagnostic: now reports usable PIT records per period (catching empty strings), so it
moves 0/N -> N/N usable; guards put_data so a pre-fix NaT rejection is surfaced.

Regression evals (real-shaped, empty-string Publish Date — not just the NaT fixture):
blank-string publish is recovered, rows pass put_data, knowledge_date > event_date,
quality populates; plus a _coerce_date unit test. Full suite: 173 passed, 4 skipped.

commit.message:
data: recover SimFin facts with missing Publish Date so quality populates (#33)

* data: recover SimFin facts with missing Publish Date so quality populates

SimFin's free bulk datasets ship "Publish Date" (a paid-tier column) empty while
"Report Date" is always present. records_from_frames dropped every row with a NaN
Publish Date at the PIT gate, so NO fundamentals reached the store and the quality
signal returned n/a for the entire universe (Piotroski/gross-profitability never
ran). Diagnosed with diagnose_simfin_quality.py: ticker + columns OK, but every
fact skipped on the missing knowledge_date.

Fix (mapping only, Piotroski math untouched): when Publish Date is absent, derive
a conservative knowledge_date = period end + filing lag (FY ~90d, quarter ~45d)
keyed off SimFin's Fiscal Period. This pushes the no-peek key strictly AFTER the
period closed — never before — so no future row can leak. A present Publish Date
still wins; only missing dates use the fallback.

Diagnostic (diagnose_simfin_quality.py): for LLY/AAPL it walks the real
records_from_frames -> store -> quality_score chain and names which of four modes
fails (ticker-key / column-name / date-knowledge_date / units). Runs on the real
.data_cache/simfin on the user's machine, falls back to a faithful fixture offline.

Evals: quality populates when Publish Date missing; the fallback knowledge_date is
no-peek safe (invisible right after year-end, visible after the lag); a present
Publish Date is unchanged; filing-lag-by-period; and the diagnostic correctly
labels all four modes. Full suite: 171 passed, 4 skipped.

commit.message:
universe: fix cache poisoning + bound the hanging EDGAR classification fetch (#32)

BUG 1 (cache poisoning): only a genuine SIC classification is written to the
store. A fetch that errors, times out, or returns empty is quarantined and left
uncached, so a re-run retries it instead of reading "kept 0" from a poisoned
cache. Restructured classify_and_cache to cache strictly on the success branch.

BUG 2 (SSL read hang): each per-ticker EDGAR fetch now runs under a hard
wall-clock deadline on a daemon thread (a parked thread can never block process
exit) with a small retry; on persistent failure the ticker is counted as
"failed" and the loop continues — a single hung SSL read can no longer stall the
whole build until Ctrl+C. Also pass EDGAR an explicit (connect, read) timeout
tuple so the read timeout fires reliably at the HTTP layer.

Evals (land with the logic): (a) a failed/empty fetch is NOT cached and IS
retried on re-run; (b) a simulated fetch timeout increments "failed" and the
loop continues to the next ticker. Full suite: 166 passed, 4 skipped.

commit.message:
universe build: incremental cache + progress + resumable (scale to ~3000 tickers)

Problem
-------
classify_and_cache classified every ticker via a sequential EDGAR /submissions
call and wrote the SIC records in ONE batch at the end, with no progress output.
At ~3000 tickers a real build grinds silently for hours and a crash/restart loses
ALL progress. The classification logic and SIC ranges are correct — only the
EXECUTION needed fixing.

Solution (classification logic + SIC ranges UNCHANGED)
------------------------------------------------------
universe/hc_tech.py:
- INCREMENTAL CACHE: each ticker's SIC is persisted to the store the moment it is
  computed (_cache_one -> put_data per ticker), not batched at the end. A re-run
  skips any already-cached ticker (cache read first; EDGAR only for unknowns), so
  the build is a resumable, one-time cost. New refresh= flag forces re-fetch.
- PROGRESS LOGGING: INFO line every log_every (default 50) tickers:
  "classified N/TOTAL (kept K hc+tech, skipped S, failed F)". Never silent.
- RATE-LIMIT DISCIPLINE: uses the passed (shared) EdgarClient, whose throttle +
  429-Retry-After govern the rate; per-ticker failures (timeout/4xx/parse) are
  quarantined and the build continues; running failed count is logged.
- limit= caps the symbols processed (smoke test). ClassifyResult gains n_kept
  (in-scope hc+tech count).

run.py: --refresh-universe and --universe-limit N flags wired into ranking mode
(symbols capped before classify + rank; refresh forwarded to classify_and_cache).

get_data remains the only data path for downstream signals; this changes only how
the universe is BUILT and cached.

Testing (evals)
---------------
- resumability: classify a fixture set, then re-run with a FRESH mock client and
  assert ZERO EDGAR calls (read entirely from cache).
- incremental persistence: an unexpected error mid-build leaves earlier tickers
  already cached (batch-at-end would lose them).
- refresh forces re-fetch despite cache; --universe-limit caps processing;
  progress logging emits the N/TOTAL/kept/skipped/failed line.
- existing classification + point-in-time + boundary tests stay green (n_kept
  asserted alongside).
- Full suite: 151 passed, 4 skipped (network) offline.

Refs ARCHITECTURE.md §1, §2.2, §5, §6.

purge/embargo" because run_walk_forward's per-slice floor defaults to ~20 and
every slice was skipped. Add a --min-obs-per-slice CLI flag that overrides the

commit.message:
edgar_client: throttle ~8 req/s + retry 429 honoring Retry-After

Problem
-------
Form 4 runs hit 429 Too Many Requests from SEC on index.json/.xml fetches. The
throttle was set at the 10 req/s limit (no margin), and a 429 was retried only
with generic exponential backoff (Retry-After ignored) — and if retries exhausted,
the filing was quarantined as if "bad", when 429 just means "slow down".

Solution
--------
data/edgar_client.py:
- MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS 0.1 -> 0.125 (~8 req/s, margin under SEC's ~10/s). The
  throttle already covers EVERY SEC call: get_json AND get_text both go through
  the single _get()/_throttle(), so index.json and .xml fetches are throttled
  (added a test asserting get_text is throttled, to settle the "bypass" concern).
- 429 is explicitly retryable: _backoff_seconds() honors the server's Retry-After
  header on a 429 (delta-seconds), falling back to exponential backoff when absent
  or an HTTP-date. Other errors keep exponential backoff. Still fails loud
  (EdgarHTTPError) only after exhausting retries.

Scope: EDGAR client throttle/backoff only. (FRED uses a similar pattern; a 429
there is a possible follow-up. Sharing one client across tickers in _ingest for a
global rate bound is a separate follow-up.)

Testing
-------
- 429-then-success honoring Retry-After: backs off by the header value (2s, not the
  exponential 1s) and recovers — not quarantined; session called twice.
- 429 without Retry-After -> exponential backoff fallback.
- throttle covers get_text (the .xml path), not just get_json.
- default min-interval is >= 0.125 (under 10/s).
- existing retry/throttle/parse tests still pass.
- Full suite: 133 passed, 4 skipped (network) offline.

Refs ARCHITECTURE.md §5.

commit.message:
form4: fetch the real ownership XML via index.json; window-bound; loud-fail

Problem
-------
The adapter built the document URL from submissions' primaryDocument, which for a
Form 4 is the XSL-rendered HTML view — so every fetch returned non-XML and every
filing was quarantined (hundreds for NVDA). It also pulled a company's ENTIRE
filing history regardless of the run's date window.

Solution
--------
data/form4.py:
- _ownership_xml_url(): resolve the RAW ownership XML inside each filing via the
  filing's index.json (pick the .xml member, preferring primary_doc/form4/
  ownership-named files), instead of fetching primaryDocument's HTML render.
- Date-window bound: fetch_insider_buys(start, end) filters filings to those whose
  filing date falls in the run window; run._ingest passes its window. A ticker
  with filings but none in window -> "no_form4_filings_in_window" (not an error).
- Loud failure: if a ticker has in-window filings but parses ZERO ownership XMLs,
  log.error (likely an adapter/URL bug) rather than only silently quarantining.
- Per-filing resilience (fetch/non-XML/ParseError -> quarantine, skip) preserved.

Scope: Form 4 URL/window/logging. run._ingest passes start/end to fetch_insider_buys.

Testing
-------
- _ownership_xml_url picks the .xml, not the XSL/HTML render (real URL structure).
- golden: a valid filing resolved via index.json parses and produces a P-buy
  record (value=owner CIK, filing-lag knowledge_date).
- window: a 2021-03-10 filing is excluded by a [2021-01-01, 2021-02-28] window;
  only the in-window valid filing is processed.
- all-non-XML -> log.error emitted (caplog).
- malformed/non-XML/P-disposal/no-filings behaviors retained.
- Full suite: 129 passed, 4 skipped (network) offline.

commit.message:
form4: per-filing parse resilience + non-XML guard; surface quarantines in ingest

Problem
-------
parse_form4 used ET.fromstring with no error handling, so a single malformed
Form 4 (mismatched tag) or a non-XML response (SEC error/HTML page) raised
ET.ParseError out of fetch_insider_buys. That error is NOT in the ingest
try/except tuple (UnknownTickerError, EdgarHTTPError), so one bad filing aborted
the whole run. Real EDGAR data will have occasional malformed/odd filings.

Solution
--------
data/form4.py:
- Per-filing resilience in fetch_insider_buys: wrap each filing's fetch+parse. A
  fetch failure (EdgarHTTPError), a non-XML response, or a ParseError quarantines
  THAT filing (recorded in Form4Result.gaps, naming the accession + reason) and is
  skipped — a ticker's other good filings still ingest; never fatal.
- Non-XML guard: _looks_like_form4_xml() detects responses lacking an
  ownershipDocument element (HTML/error pages) and quarantines them instead of
  feeding them to the XML parser.
- Parser hardening: parse_form4 handles namespaces explicitly (compares local tag
  names, stripping any {namespace} prefix) and documents that it raises ParseError
  on malformed XML for the caller to catch per filing.
- run._ingest now captures fetch_insider_buys().gaps into the ingest quarantine
  (defensively via getattr), so per-filing quarantines reach
  RunResult.ingest_quarantine. The ticker-level try/except still catches
  UnknownTickerError/EdgarHTTPError.

Scope: Form 4 parse resilience only.

Testing
-------
- one valid Form 4 + one malformed XML (two filings): the valid one parses and
  produces the open-market buy; the malformed one is quarantined (form4_parse_error
  + accession); not fatal.
- non-XML (HTML error page) -> quarantined (form4_non_xml_response), not parsed.
- parse_form4 still raises ET.ParseError on malformed input (pure parser).
- Full suite: 126 passed, 4 skipped (network) offline.

Refs ARCHITECTURE.md §2, §5.

commit.message:
run._ingest: per-ticker resilience for prices, fundamentals, and Form 4

Problem
-------
_ingest fetched prices/fundamentals in a bare loop, so a single ticker's failure
(a delisted name with no free data, or a transient yfinance/Stooq/EDGAR error)
aborted the entire run. The full survivorship-free universe will contain such
names by design — brittle ingest makes the harness unusable on real universes.
(Form 4 wasn't ingested at all.)

Solution
--------
run.py _ingest:
- Wrap each per-ticker fetch in try/except. On a per-ticker failure, record the
  ticker in the quarantine list (evals.coverage shape: ticker/field/reason/vendor)
  and continue to the next ticker:
  * prices: catch DataPullError -> field "close".
  * fundamentals: catch (UnknownTickerError, EdgarHTTPError) -> field "fundamentals".
  * Form 4 (newly wired into ingest): catch the same -> field "form4_buy_P".
- Only raise PipelineError if ZERO universe tickers ingest a price.
- Config errors (e.g. EdgarConfigError from a missing SEC User-Agent) still
  propagate — that is setup, not a per-ticker data gap.
- The benchmark price is quarantined (not fatal) if it fails; the labeler surfaces
  the gap downstream.
- _ingest returns the quarantine; run() exposes it as RunResult.ingest_quarantine.

Scope: ingest resilience only. (FRED macro ingest remains a separate follow-up.)

Testing
-------
- one good ticker + one unresolvable ticker: the good ticker (and benchmark)
  ingest; the bad ticker is quarantined for all three sources (price/fundamentals/
  form4) each with a reason; the good ticker is never quarantined; the run proceeds.
- zero priced tickers -> PipelineError (fail loud).
- Offline (prices/fundamentals/form4 monkeypatched). Full suite: 123 passed,
  4 skipped (network).

Refs ARCHITECTURE.md §2, §5.

Fix benchmark symbol: NASDAQ_COMP -> ^IXIC, with per-provider index mapping

Problem
-------
The Nasdaq benchmark was the placeholder "NASDAQ_COMP", which is not a valid
yfinance/Stooq symbol, so the benchmark price fetch fails and the labeler can't
grade any ticker (every outcome becomes not-yet-known -> the run fails).

--------

  Nasdaq Composite). It flows through the store and labeler unchanged.
- data/prices.py: yfinance takes ^IXIC directly, but Stooq codes indices
  differently (no ".us" equity suffix). Add STOOQ_INDEX_SYMBOLS + _stooq_symbol():
  ^IXIC -> ^ndq, ^GSPC -> ^spx, ^DJI -> ^dji; other ^-symbols fall back to a
  lowercased form; US equities keep the ".us" suffix. _from_stooq now uses it.

  so the orchestrator tests follow the symbol.

Problem

purchases as point-in-time records, but no adapter feeds them, so the signal is

  (guarded by a test).

Problem

ARCHITECTURE.md §5/§6: the macro regime gate needs HY OAS, Fed funds rate and VIX
as point-in-time series, but no adapter feeds them, so the gate is not_run. They

- FredClient: throttled, retrying JSON client for the FRED observations API.
  Required, configurable API key (STOCKSCOPE_FRED_API_KEY env or arg;
  FredConfigError if unset). Retry/backoff + throttle mirror data/edgar_client.py.

  knowledge_date = observation date + a documented per-series publication lag

  skipped; a series with no usable observations is flagged as a coverage gap,
  never zeroed. Field names match macro.regime (guarded by a test).

commit.message:
run.py orchestrator: wire the end-to-end pipeline (plain Python, no LLM)

Problem
-------
ARCHITECTURE.md §5/§7 call for a plain-Python sequencer (never an LLM) that runs
the harness end to end. Until now run.py was a stub; the stages existed but
nothing wired them, so there was no `python run.py`.

Solution
--------
run.py:
- run(RunConfig) sequences: optional ingest (live adapters) -> resolve universe
  per entry date -> score active signals per (ticker x date) -> label outcomes
  (sanctioned labeler, cached per ticker/date) -> assemble a Pandera-validated
  observation frame per signal -> walk-forward (two-arm per slice) -> build_report
  -> write report.md.
- Fail loud, never fake: a signal whose data ADAPTER is not wired is marked
  not_run (distinct from insufficient_data = adapter exists but the store lacks
  data). If no signal is runnable, or none yields an evaluable result (e.g.
  benchmark absent -> all labels not-yet-known), run() raises PipelineError rather
  than emit a verdict on data it doesn't have - no report is written.
- Config-driven scope (RunConfig: tickers, entry dates, active signals,
  thresholds) so a tiny slice scales up with no code change. Signal scorers are
  injectable; DEFAULT_SIGNALS wires the real signals (momentum/quality have live
  adapters -> runnable; revisions/insiders have none yet -> not_run).
- main() is a thin CLI building a RunConfig and calling run().

Scope: orchestration only; no signal/stat logic changed. Updates the scaffold CLI
test (main is wired now) to assert --help parses.

Testing
-------
- end-to-end on a small synthetic store -> complete report + GO verdict written to
  disk (two planted-edge archetypes confirm).
- partial readiness (quality active, revisions/insiders no adapter) -> quality
  evaluated, others not_run, report produced, no crash; a not_run signal's scorer
  is never called.
- fail loud: missing benchmark -> PipelineError, no report.md written; all-active
  signals lacking an adapter -> PipelineError.
- default registry adapter-availability contract.
- Full suite: 102 passed, 2 skipped (network) offline.

Refs ARCHITECTURE.md §5, §7, §9.

EDGAR fundamentals adapter (data.sec.gov) — feeds the quality signal

Problem
-------
ARCHITECTURE.md §5/§6 deferred the EDGAR source from the data-layer PR. The
quality signal needs real point-in-time fundamentals (9 us-gaap concepts), pulled
honestly: SEC requires a contact User-Agent (403 without it), fair-access
throttling, restatement-aware point-in-time records, and fail-loud on unknown
tickers / missing concepts.

Solution
--------
data/edgar_client.py:
- EdgarClient: thin JSON client for data.sec.gov. Required, CONFIGURABLE
  User-Agent (STOCKSCOPE_SEC_USER_AGENT env or arg; EdgarConfigError if unset -
  contact info, not a secret). Throttles to <=10 req/s and reuses the
  retry/exponential-backoff pattern from data/prices.py (session/sleep/clock
  injectable for tests).
- CikResolver: fetches company_tickers.json once, caches ticker -> zero-padded
  10-digit CIK; UnknownTickerError on a miss (never guesses).

data/fundamentals.py:
- fetch_fundamentals(ticker): pulls companyfacts and extracts the 9 us-gaap
  concepts (NetIncomeLoss, NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities, Assets,
  LongTermDebtNoncurrent, AssetsCurrent, LiabilitiesCurrent,
  CommonStockSharesOutstanding, GrossProfit, Revenues), each with a documented
  fallback tag list. Maps each fact to a universal record (value, event_date=end,
  knowledge_date=filed, source="edgar") and writes via the existing put_data so
  Pandera validation + fail-loud apply. A concept with no matching tag is flagged
  as a coverage gap, never zeroed. The 9 target fields match signals.quality.FIELDS
  (guarded by a test).
- Restatements: every (value, filed) is kept as a separate record - never
  collapsed to latest - so the store's knowledge_date filter returns the version
  known as-of any query date.

stub remains a documented follow-up.

-------

  extract to exact values with correct event_date/knowledge_date/source.
- fallback tag used when the primary is absent.
- missing concept -> coverage gap, not zeroed.
- CIK resolution (zero-pad, case-insensitive, fetched once/cached); unknown
  ticker fails loud.
- missing User-Agent fails loud; throttle waits the remainder between requests;
  get_json retries then succeeds.
- restatement: two facts same period/different filed -> both kept; an as-of-original

- alignment: CONCEPTS fields == signals.quality.FIELDS (drift guard).

PR 12 (§9.12): walk-forward evaluation with purge + embargo

Problem
-------
ARCHITECTURE.md §3/§10 require the edge to hold across >=3 distinct years, not as
a single pooled number that could be driven by one lucky year. And §2's no-leakage
non-negotiable applies to time: 12-month labels can leak across slice boundaries,
and overlapping labels can inflate aggregate significance by double-counting.

Solution
--------
backtest/walk_forward.py:
- run_walk_forward(observations) slices by entry year, runs the §9.11 two-arm
  engine per slice, and reports lift/CI/rank-IC per year plus an aggregate
  (mean/median lift, fraction of slices positive/significant, mean rank-IC, and a
  >=3-year consistency verdict). The distribution of the edge over time, not a
  pooled point estimate.
- purge_embargo(): PURGE drops observations whose 12-month window strictly
  straddles a year boundary (outcome spans two slices -> backward leakage); with
  annual Jan-1 entries the windows are adjacent so clean entries survive while
  intra-year observations are purged. EMBARGO additionally drops observations
  within embargo_days after a boundary or whose window ends within embargo_days
  before one (residual autocorrelation). Documented as §2-applied-to-time.
- Overlap-aware counting: we do NOT pool overlapping labels into one test; each
  YEAR is the independent unit, significance is per-slice + >=3-year consistency,
  and raw vs kept counts are reported so the de-overlapping is explicit.
- Fail loud: no evaluable slices raises rather than returning a silent empty.

Scope: walk-forward runner only. Retargets the scaffold "stubs raise" test from
backtest.run_walk_forward to the still-stubbed report.build_report (PR 13).

Testing
-------
- consistent lift across 7 years -> all slices positive, >=3 significant,
  consistent True; both arms reported per slice.
- one-year-only lift -> exactly 1 significant-positive year -> consistent False
  (the discipline catches the fluke).
- purge/embargo -> mid-year (boundary-crossing) rows removed, effective N shrinks
  to the Jan-1 entries only.
- zero-lift -> ~0 mean lift, 0 significant-positive years, consistent False.
- Full suite: 77 passed, 1 skipped (network) offline.

Refs ARCHITECTURE.md §2, §3, §10, §9.12.

commit.message:
PR 11 (§9.11): two-arm stats engine + calibration eval

Problem
-------
ARCHITECTURE.md §2.3 forbids a winners-only view: every signal must be judged
P(winner | fired) vs the base rate, with same-signal losers explicitly counted.
§3 sets the bar: the conditional lift's CI must exclude zero. §9.11 schedules the
engine + its calibration eval. The engine must also never count outcomes that
aren't known yet, and must not manufacture an edge that isn't there.

Solution
--------
stats/two_arm.py:
- two_arm_lift(observations) validates a tidy (ticker x as_of) frame against a
  Pandera schema carrying the deferred range asserts (score in [0,100], is_winner
  in {True,False,None}); is_winner dtype is intentionally unpinned (bool when
  complete, object when it carries None).
- Drops not_yet_known labels (and score-less rows) up front - never counted as a
  win or loss.
- Computes BOTH arms always: base_rate, p_fired = P(winner|fired), p_not_fired
  (loser arm), lift = p_fired - base_rate, plus lift_vs_not_fired. Fired = score
  >= threshold (default top quantile q=0.8, documented).
- CI via seeded percentile bootstrap on the lift (deterministic); p-value via a
  two-proportion z-test (fired vs not-fired); rank-IC via Spearman(score, excess).
- Two-arm enforcement is structural: TwoArmResult always carries base_rate + both
  arms; there is no fired-arm-only summary. An empty arm or no-labels fails loud.

evals/calibration.py (the validity test, §8):
- synthetic_observations() plants a known lift (fired 0.70 vs base 0.50 -> 0.20).
- assert_recovers_planted_lift: lift ~0.20 within CI, CI excludes zero, rank-IC>0.
- assert_zero_lift_not_significant (non-vacuity): a deterministically balanced
  zero-lift set -> lift ~0, CI straddles zero, p-value not significant. Balanced
  (not random) so non-significance is robust, not a flaky draw from the null.

Testing
-------
- unit: hand-checkable two-arm (p_fired 0.8, base 0.5, p_not_fired 0.2, lift 0.3);
  unknown labels dropped (and all-unknown fails loud); score>100 and invalid
  is_winner rejected by the schema; empty arm fails loud.
- calibration across seeds {0,1,7}: planted lift recovered + significant with
  rank-IC>0; zero-lift reported ~0 and non-significant.
- Full suite: 73 passed, 1 skipped (network) offline.

Refs ARCHITECTURE.md §2, §3, §8, §9.11.

PR 10 (§9.10): winner labeler (12m total return vs Nasdaq, >=15pp) + golden case

Problem
-------
ARCHITECTURE.md §3 defines the winner: beat the Nasdaq Composite total return by
>=15pp over the next 12 months. §9.10 schedules the labeler. A label legitimately
uses the future (it is the answer key), but that look-ahead must be quarantined to
the labeler and never conflated with the signal path - the subtlest possible bug.

Solution
--------
backtest/labels.py (the ONE sanctioned look-ahead, never called by signals):
- label_winner(ticker, as_of) reads close prices via store.get_data, but queries
  the store AS OF horizon_end (as_of + 12 months) - the only deliberate use of a
  later as_of. Excess = ticker_return - benchmark_return; winner = excess >= 15pp
  (inclusive >=). Heavily documented quarantine boundary.
- Incomplete-future guard keyed on the BENCHMARK (the index always trades): if the
  benchmark has no close within tolerance of horizon_end, the window hasn't
  elapsed -> outcome_not_yet_known (never a premature/partial label).
- Delisting = disaster, not unknown: if the benchmark window elapsed but the
  ticker stopped trading mid-window, model it as a total loss (exit 0 -> -100%).
- backtest/__init__ re-exports label_winner; run_walk_forward stays a stub (PR 12).

- delisted-to-zero: last close mid-window, benchmark elapsed -> exit 0, -100%

- incomplete window: horizon beyond benchmark data -> outcome_not_yet_known, None.

PR 9 (§9.9): macro regime gate (HY OAS + Fed + VIX -> risk-off AND gate)

Problem
-------
ARCHITECTURE.md §4 locks a macro gate: risk-off -> cash when HY OAS widening AND
Fed tightening hard AND VIX regime breaking. §9.9 schedules it. It must be an AND
(coinciding stress, not any single fire), point-in-time (FRED release lag), and
must NOT silently assume risk-on when data is missing.

Solution
--------
macro/regime.py (reads ONLY via store.get_data):
- regime_state(as_of) returns a RegimeState: state ("risk_off"/"risk_on"), a
  boolean gate_closed (True => cash), the three condition booleans, and raw
  values - not a 0-100 score.
- Conditions over a trailing window (default 63d): HY OAS widening >= 1.0pp; Fed
  policy rate up >= 0.5pp (tightening hard); VIX >= 30 or a >= 10pt spike.
- AND gate: risk_off = widening AND tightening AND vix_break. Documented so it is
  unambiguously AND, not OR.
- PIT model: macro series stored under the sentinel ticker MACRO with event_date =
  data date, knowledge_date = release date; store filters knowledge_date <= as_of.
- Safe default: if any required series is missing/too short, fail SAFE to risk-off
  (gate closed), set insufficient_data, and name the missing series via
  macro_coverage_gaps() - never silently assume risk-on (staying invested while
  blind is the dangerous default).

Scope: macro gate only. Retargets the scaffold "stubs raise" test from
macro.regime to the still-stubbed backtest.label_winner (PR 10).

Testing
-------
- all conditions coincide -> gate closed (risk_off).
- benign macro -> gate open (risk_on).
- single condition (VIX only) -> gate STAYS OPEN, exactly one condition fired
  (proves AND, not OR).
- missing series (VIX absent) -> insufficient_data, fail-safe gate closed.
- release-lag no-leak: a spike released after as_of does not flip the gate until
  its release date; reuse PR-3 assert_no_future_rows over the macro series.
- Full suite: 57 passed, 1 skipped (network) offline.

Problem

non-routine)"; §9.7 schedules it. It must count only genuine open-market
purchases (Form 4 code P), exclude exercises/grants/sells (M/A/S), respect the

Solution

signals/insider.py (reads ONLY via store.get_data; renames the scaffold stub
signals/insiders.py):

Problem

PR 4: survivorship-free universe + liquidity filter

Problem
-------
ARCHITECTURE.md §7/§9.4 need a universe layer that, for any historical date,
returns the Nasdaq healthcare+tech names that were actually tradable then —
including names later delisted (§2 survivorship-free) — without reading raw data

get_data chokepoint is per-ticker (can't enumerate symbols) and the record
schema's value is float-only (can't hold a categorical sector).

PR 3: data-integrity eval layer — hard no-peek, coverage/survivorship, filing-lag, adapter resilience

Problem
-------
PR 2 gave us the chokepoint and a write-time schema, but ARCHITECTURE.md §2/§8
demand the integrity guarantees be *enforced by automated checks, not trust*:
a hard leak test (not just one unit case), a fail-loud coverage/survivorship
report that quarantines gaps, a filing-lag guarantee, schemas on every store
boundary, and a price adapter that survives flaky vendors without silent drops.

Solution
--------
- evals/no_peek.py: assert_no_future_rows() fuzzes a grid of (field, ticker,
  as_of) probes and raises LeakError (failing the build) on ANY row with
  knowledge_date > as_of — naming the exact offender.
- evals/coverage.py: coverage_report() reports fetched X of Y, names each gap by
  vendor/ticker/field, quarantines missing cells, and renders a human-readable
  coverage matrix. A known-delisted fixture proves dead names are detectable,
  not silently absent (survivorship intent).
- store/store.py: Pandera schema now also guards the READ boundary (non-empty
  results), so every frame leaving the store satisfies the universal record.
- data/prices.py: retry + exponential backoff + polite throttle per provider;
  on exhaustion raises DataPullError carrying a quarantine map (provider ->
  reason) — never returns empty silently. sleep is injectable for tests.

Scope: real EDGAR filing-lag wiring is deferred to the EDGAR adapter PR (§9);
this proves the store honours whatever knowledge_date ingest assigns.

Testing
-------
- no-peek (hard): fuzzed grid over 2 years x 3 tickers passes; a deliberately
  leaky store makes the checker raise (proves it bites).
- coverage: counts, quarantine, delisted-name detectability, matrix rendering.
- filing-lag: Q1 (event 03-31) invisible until 10-Q filing (knowledge 05-15).
- adapter resilience: retries-then-succeeds (backoff [1,2]), fallback to Stooq,
  and exhaustion raises with both providers quarantined — all with fake sleep,
  no network.
- Full suite: 26 passed, 1 skipped (network) offline.

Refs ARCHITECTURE.md §2 (non-negotiables), §8 (eval layers), §9 PR 3.

commit.message:
PR 2: data-layer spine — point-in-time store + get_data chokepoint + price adapter

Problem
-------
The harness has no way to store or read data, and ARCHITECTURE.md §2/§6 require
that EVERY read go through one chokepoint that filters knowledge_date <= as_of.
Without that contract — and a validated write path — no signal can be trusted
not to peek, and malformed rows could silently corrupt the experiment.

Solution
--------
- store/schema.py: the universal point-in-time record (ticker, field, value,
  event_date, knowledge_date, source) with a Pandera schema (strict=True,
  lazy=True, coerce=True) used to validate every write.
- store/store.py: a SQLite-backed PITStore.
  * put_data(records) validates against the schema before insert and raises
    loudly on failure — no silent/partial drops.
  * get_data(field, ticker, as_of) is the chokepoint: the knowledge_date <= as_of
    predicate lives in SQL, returns newest event_date first; no path bypasses it.
  * DB path configurable; defaults to gitignored .data_cache/store.sqlite, not
    the data/ source package.
- data/prices.py: first adapter, fetch_prices(ticker, start, end) — daily closes
  from yfinance with a Stooq fallback; fail-loud DataPullError on empty/failed
  pulls. Price bars carry no filing lag, so event_date == knowledge_date.
- store/__init__.py re-exports the chokepoint so callers depend on `store`.

Scope: EDGAR / FRED / Form 4 sources are deferred to later PRs (§9).

Testing
-------
- no-peek: a row known on 2020-06-15 is invisible as_of 2020-06-14, visible on
  06-15 (tests/test_store.py).
- schema: malformed (missing column / wrong type) record raises on put_data.
- ordering: get_data returns newest event_date first.
- adapter smoke: fetch_prices returns >=1 schema-valid record (marked `network`,
  skips cleanly offline).
- Full suite: 16 passed, 1 skipped (network) offline.

Refs ARCHITECTURE.md §6 (data-access contract), §8 (eval layers), §9 PR 2.
